candidates.summary: Cursor shipped Build Live Apps: cloud agents can scaffold a web app, provision Postgres and Cursor-SSO auth, run deterministic plus agentic security checks, and publish a shareable link so tools leave localhost; available on all paid plans with cloud agents enabled.
facts: Cursor changelog and @cursor_ai (2026-11-05): describe the tool; Cursor builds, sets up a database, configures auth, and deploys; publish picks a unique domain and returns a live link.

Guardrails: deterministic and agentic security checks catch secrets in app files / exposed credentials; nothing goes live until checks pass and the user explicitly publishes; team admins can see every app and secret, add review rules, approve blocked publishes, and unpublish.
Sharing: specific people, groups, or entire team behind Cursor sign-in; individual plans can also share publicly; Cursor API key can let a script or Grok Bot call the app.

Repos/GitHub supported; GitLab coming; @rauchg and Vercel noted one-click deploy built on Vercel for Platforms; internal Cursor teams already using it for ops tools, customer demos, onboarding, sales dashboards, and engineering portals.

related.name: Guillermo Rauch on the build-deploy-distribute loop

candidates.summary: Anthropic launched Personal Finance in Claude (US beta on Pro/Max/Ultra): users connect bank and card accounts via Plaid for read-only balances and up to two years of transactions, and Claude answers money questions in everyday language without moving funds or giving investment advice.
facts: Anthropic article and @claudeai (2026-11-05): access is read-only; Claude cannot move, manage, or invest money; no ads or sponsored recommendations; not designed to give investment advice.

Via Plaid the user signs into the bank; Claude does not see banking passwords; for connected accounts Claude sees bank name, account name/type/last four digits, balances and credit limits, and up to two years of transactions.
Example flows: 'Where did my money go this month?' with category breakdown; bills left before payday; whether a trip is affordable; charts and calendars the user can adjust.

Personal Finance hub chats are not used to train models; accounts can be unlinked anytime; Anthropic says it is exploring working alongside licensed professionals and wants banks/wealth managers to help shape next steps. Verge coverage same day.

candidates.summary: Perplexity launched Teammates — always-on work agents that take jobs using Computer projects/skills/memory, collaborate with other teammates, and message coworkers in Slack; Max ($200/mo) web preview today, with CEO Aravind Srinivas saying ~10,000 teammates ran internally in 30 days (~20× headcount).
facts: @perplexity_ai (2026-11-05): Teammates work proactively from existing Projects, skills, and memory in Computer; each gets its own thread; available now for Max subscribers on the web.

@AravSrinivas: about 10,000 teammates in Perplexity's internal workspace in the last 30 days (~20× headcount); about 1,000 active yesterday; 'Headcount growth and planning will be done very differently in the coming years.'
Verge: positioned against OpenAI Dots and Claude Duet; builds on Perplexity Computer for ongoing large-scale work; Slack interaction supported; more expensive because it requires Max.

Quoted Johnny Hwin note: research preview for Max; intended for deep research, data analysis, QA, triaging tickets, reviewing code; teammates close their own loops rather than needing repeated session steering.

related.name: Aravind Srinivas on internal Teammates count

candidates.summary: A Claude Code GitHub issue (HN 201) reports the harness put the user's email in the User-Agent header on web requests during searches; an Anthropic commenter says built-in mod cc-plugin-privacy in v2.1.317+ blocks the behavior by default (toggleable via /plugins).
facts: GitHub issue #107757 opened 2026-11-05 by taylor-edwards against anthropics/claude-code (labels bug, area:security, area:tools); reporter on macOS Claude Code 2.1.318 says email was sent to third parties in User-Agent during web searches without permission.
HN discussion 'Claude Code sends your email address to websites' reached 201 points the same evening.

Comment from poteat (2026-11-05): built-in mod cc-plugin-privacy introduced to deterministically block this in v2.1.317 and later; enabled by default; can be turned off via /plugins; plans to publish the mod source like other built-ins.
Issue also references #101659 about a subagent sending the user's email from session context in a User-Agent header.

candidates.summary: Nous Research released Hermes Agent v0.23.0 (Hearth): Desktop workspace in a browser tab from your own gateway, one gateway owning every conversation across CLI/TUI/Desktop/bots/cron, /Rewind, Group Chats with automatic routing, spend limits on paid MCP tools, and latency/memory work for long-lived gateways.
facts: GitHub release and @NousResearch (2026-11-05): since v0.22.0 ~10,080 commits, ~1,950 merged PRs, ~850 issues closed, 666 contributors; rolls up v0.22.1–v0.22.7 patch notes.
Webapp serves full Desktop workspace from the gateway (off by default; webapp.enabled / Web Access); one gateway per machine owns sessions so surfaces stop double-writing.

Other highlights: Esc Esc or /Rewind to edit/fork earlier prompts; Group Chat lead-bot or auto router; paid MCP tools show price and chat spend limits even in YOLO; plugin catalog ~600 → 1,050+ with a Verified tier; pluggable delegation including advanced-delegation plugin.
Breaking: old browser_* tools removed in favor of browser_exec; Desktop needs macOS 13+ / 64-bit Windows (Electron 44); hermes mcp serve → hermes mcp-serve plugin.

candidates.summary: LangChain published Agents Are Going Async and shipped async subagents in Deep Agents (Python/JS) and Managed Deep Agents: an orchestrator stays responsive while background subagents run long work and report back, with start/check/update/cancel/list tools and interrupt vs enqueue steering.
facts: LangChain blog by Sydney Runkle and Thushanth Bengre (2026-11-05); promoted by @LangChain and @hwchase17 (Harrison: most agents LangChain builds internally already leverage async subagents).
Pattern framed against blocked ReAct loops; cites Claude Code background subagents, OpenAI Dots background workers, and DeepSeek Harness router + workers.
Orchestrator tools: start_async_task, check_async_task, update_async_task, cancel_async_task, list_async_tasks; update_strategy interrupt (default) vs enqueue.
Managed Deep Agents: set "async": True on a subagent; every served agent also gets an async general-purpose subagent; task notifications in beta; sample repo async-deep-agents.

candidates.summary: Naval argues actual progress comes from hard-to-build technology, which comes from competitive creative free-market capitalism in one small precarious area that then diffuses worldwide — and that snuffing that out means global stagnation for a very long time.
facts: @naval post 2026-11-05: 'Actual progress comes from hard-to-build technology. Which comes from competitive, creative, free-market capitalism. Which comes from one small, precarious area and then diffuses to the rest of the world. Snuff that out, and it’s global stagnation for an extremely long time.'
Frontier-capital lane; original view post (not a market tip).

candidates.summary: Lyn Alden, tying to recent AI hacking news, argues that keeping nuclear codes, air-traffic, and core bank systems on offline rarely updated media is not the worst design — security and maintenance beat frequent innovation for existential systems she saw firsthand at the FAA.
facts: @LynAldenContact thread 2026-11-05: TL;DR that nuclear codes, air traffic, and core bank systems on offline floppy drives that never updated is 'not the worst thing, given the increasing era of hacking.'

Earlier in thread: nuclear systems stayed on that tech until ~2019; FAA is phasing out now; 'Super-secure slow-update tech like nuclear, air traffic, or banking, doesn't want to touch the outside world for as long as possible.'
Source note: she worked 12 years at the FAA simulation division for new technology; when existential systems update it needs extreme vetting; old isolated maintained tech can be good.
Explicitly frames the view against recent AI hacking headlines.
